sentences.text: Estimates for the size of this dinosaur vary significantly. Buffetaut estimated the length of Siamotyrannus at seven meters. In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 6 meters and the weight at 500 kg. In 2016, Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated the length at 10 meters and the weight at 1.75 tonnes.
The second and third sacral vertebrae are strongly transversely flattened.
A partial skeleton of a large theropod was found in 1993 at the Phu Wiang 9 site in Khon Kaen by Somchai Traimwichanon.
The species Siamotyrannus isanensis was named and described in 1996 by Eric Buffetaut, Varavudh Suteethorn, and Haiyan Tong.
The holotype specimen PW9-1 was found in the Sao Khua Formation dating from the Berriasian to Barremian stages.
Fossils of Siamotyrannus consist of a pelvis and vertebrae found in Thailand within the Sao Khua Formation.

Siamotyrannus isanensis is the only known species of the extinct genus Siamotyrannus, a metriacanthosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous between 129 and 113 million years ago in what is now Asia.
Although originally thought to be a tyrannosauroid or tyrannosaurid, its position in that group is uncertain due to lacking primary defining traits.
In 2012, Matthew Carrano et al. placed Siamotyrannus in the Metriacanthosaurinae.
In a 2024 review, Cau recovered Siamotyrannus as a tetanuran outside the Orionides and a close relative of Siamraptor.
The parent group of Siamotyrannus is Metriacanthosaurinae, and it belongs to the family Metriacanthosauridae.
Siamotyrannus lived during the Barremian stage, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
